target_customer: Emerging food and beverage CPG brands that sell through retailers and distributors and lack a data team
problem: Small CPG brands download retailer and distributor portal data by hand and stitch it into spreadsheets to see velocity, distribution and inventory.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for analytics and reporting

founders.name: Andres Recalde
founders.background_notes: YC page lists these employers for him; a search summary attributed them the other way round, so the split is uncertain.

founders.name: Sal Calvo
founders.background_notes: Met Recalde building data warehouses at RJMetrics.

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly connectors to retailer and distributor portals plus a warehouse and dashboards, work the founders had done before at RJMetrics. Portal scraping upkeep is the hard part.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations and standardized data create some lock-in, but the approach was copyable by better funded data platforms.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought it; a CPG finance platform, Confido, acquired it in October 2025 for an undisclosed price.

market_need_then: Emerging CPG brands relied on manual portal downloads and spreadsheets for store-level sales and inventory, per the YC launch post and the company site.

branding.domain_note: Uses muffindata.com, an exact .com; acquisition history of the domain not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and benefit-led: clear answers, ease of use

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself found; the name is friendly but has no stated meaning and several unrelated companies share the word.

outcome_analysis: Two former RJMetrics data engineers built a narrow analytics product for emerging CPG brands and went through YC in Winter 2023. They stayed small, raised little publicly, and were acquired by Confido in October 2025 to give its CPG finance platform retail analytics. The price is undisclosed, so whether this was a strong exit or a soft landing is unknown.
notes: Funding unverified: aggregators give $500K (CB Insights), $125K (Extruct) or none (Latka); none corroborated by a second primary source, so no rounds recorded. Competitor search found only undated 2026 vendor roundups (Crisp, Alloy, Stackline), so the dated competitor list is empty.
